overview: Black sacrifices a pawn with 3...b5 for open a- and b-files, a long-term queenside initiative and a fianchettoed bishop on g7. In the main line 4.cxb5 a6 5.bxa6 Bxa6 6.Nc3 g6 Black plays ...d6, ...Bg7, ...O-O and puts rooks on the a- and b-files while White tries to consolidate with Kg2 and a solid set-up. White usually keeps the pawn but sits through long pressure.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn, consolidate with g3, Bg2 or Nf3 and Kg2/Kf1, and return the pawn at the right moment.
Break in the centre with e4 and e5 or push Black back.

black_ideas.idea: Pressure on the open a- and b-files with rooks and queen, with the g7 bishop on the long diagonal.
Trade White's central pieces, attack b2 and keep the compensation long term.

typical_structures.structure: Black with a pawn down and half-open a/b files; White with a d5/e4 centre.

character.notes: Unbalanced, long-term compensation with real risk for both sides, though not especially forcing.

gambit.notes: White can keep the pawn for a long time, at the price of passivity.

soundness.notes: Played by strong players for decades; considered sound compensation.

structure.notes: White pawns on d5 and e4 with Black half-open files; a fixed asymmetric structure.

approach.notes: A recognised weapon at top level.

level.notes: Compensation is positional and hard to judge.

character.reason: An unbalanced pawn sacrifice where both sides take risks.

gambit.reason: Black gives a pawn that White can keep.

structure.reason: Fixed asymmetric centre with half-open files for Black.

approach.reason: A regular weapon of strong players.

level.reason: Plans are clear but judging compensation is hard.

plans.reason: Bishop on g7 and pressure on the queenside.
